audit.whatIsWrong: The entry never mentions Goes Where He Pleases, Mundo's passive, anywhere in either layer. This is the single most important interaction in the matchup and it was completely absent.
audit.why: Mundo's passive resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him. Zac's entire commit pattern is displacement — Stretching Strikes, Elastic Slingshot and Let's Bounce! are all CC. If Zac opens with E or R, the passive eats it and the engage is wasted. The correct sequence is to spend a cheap CC first to pop the passive, then commit. Nothing in the entry told the player this.
audit.corrected: Bait the passive with Q or E before spending R; the first displacement you land is absorbed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heart Zapper is described as flat "sustain + reset", which misses the condition attached to its healing.
audit.why: Riot's Heart Zapper text: Mundo stores a portion of damage he takes, then bursts nearby enemies at the end of the duration or on recast, and heals a percentage of the stored damage only if the burst hit an enemy. Its range is 325. Walking out of that radius before it detonates denies the heal outright — a much more actionable answer than generic anti-heal.
audit.corrected: Leave the 325 radius before Heart Zapper detonates and he heals nothing from it.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] read "Out-sustain with passive Adrenaline heals". Mundo has no ability called Adrenaline.
audit.why: Adrenaline Rush was Mundo's passive before his 2021 rework. His current passive is Goes Where He Pleases, which is a CC-resist that drops a recoverable cannister, not a flat regen aura. The suspectNames scan did not catch this one because the string is far enough from any current ability name to fall outside its edit-distance window.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the passive's actual function: absorbing the first CC.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid instructed the player to "trade whenever his Q is down". Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4-second cooldown.
audit.why: A 4s cooldown is not a trading window — it is back up before a trade resolves. Sequencing the lane around it is unusable advice. The real windows are Heart Zapper at 17s at rank 1 and Maximum Dosage at 120s.
audit.corrected: Re-pointed the trade metronome at Heart Zapper (17s) instead of a 4s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] why read "Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight" for the Level 6 stage — boilerplate that ignores Maximum Dosage entirely while the side label says Skill.
audit.why: Level 6 in this lane is defined by Mundo's ultimate healing a percent of his missing health instantly and then regenerating over a long duration, which is what makes a solo all-in unfinishable. The stage text should say that.
audit.corrected: Rewrote to describe the actual level-6 dynamic.

audit.why: Anti-heal being called core is right here — Heart Zapper and Maximum Dosage are both healing, and Grievous Wounds is the correct item response. The existing guidance stands.

edits.after: From level 3 you take over — W Unstable Matter chunks his oversized HP bar, and Heart Zapper's 17s cooldown is the real trade window since his cleaver is only 4s; the even beat is 6 when Maximum Dosage (R) heals him through a full commit.

notes: Highest-value find in this matchup: Mundo's passive Goes Where He Pleases was absent from both layers. Since every Zac commit tool is displacement, the passive silently eats the opener unless it is baited first — the entry previously gave no hint of this. Second: wants.foe[2] referenced "passive Adrenaline heals", an ability that has not existed since Mundo's rework; the suspectNames scan missed it because the string is too far from any live ability name to trip the edit-distance check. Worth re-running that scan with a check against retired ability names, since other entries generated from the same source may carry the same class of error. Not asserted: whether Zac's Elastic Slingshot knockup counts as the immobilizing effect the passive consumes versus his Q pull — I could not verify which one the passive prioritises when both land in the same window, so the text just says spend the cheap one first.
